sentences.text: Learned counsel submits that on this sole ground, the appellant has invoked the appellate jurisdiction of this Court, and further prays that only to that limited extent the impugned cognizance order date 4.12.2021 be set aside.
No other point has been argued.

After hearing the learned counsel and considering his submissions, this Court finds that according to the complainant, on 20.9.2019 she visited the house of the appellant-Amit Yadav where he along with his three other accomplices committed rape upon her and after completion of investigation, the charge sheet against the appellant has been filed, whereas the other accomplices have not been arrested.

Since, the allegations contained in the F.I.R. pertains to the offence punishable under Section 376-D I.P.C., therefore, merely, because the other accused have not been apprehended, the impugned cognizance in respect of the alleged offences cannot be interfered with on this limited ground.

At the stage of taking cognizance of the offences, the trial court is only required to examine the final report under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C. or the complaint, as the case may be, and is not required to give detailed reasons as the cognizance order indicates the initiation of criminal proceedings in respect of the commission of alleged offences.

That apart, the final report under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C. is yet to be examined by the trial court and at that stage, the accused would also be heard, therefore, this Court is not inclined to exercise the appellate powers, as the grounds and issues raised by the appellants can also be pressed while considering the record of the case for framing of charges.
Resultantly, without meaning any expression of opinion on the merits of the case, the appeal is hereby, dismissed.
